must_remember: The macroscopic behavior of an ideal gas is governed by the equation $PV = nRT$.
Collisions between ideal gas molecules and container walls are perfectly elastic, conserving both momentum and kinetic energy.
Absolute temperature ($T$) is a direct measure of the average translational kinetic energy per molecule ($E = \frac{3}{2}kT$).
Root mean square velocity of gas molecules is given by $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\frac{3kT}{m}}$.
At absolute zero ($T = 0\text{ K}$), the average kinetic energy of gas molecules theoretically drops to zero.

glossary.meaning: A hypothetical gas that perfectly obeys the gas laws ($PV = nRT$) under all conditions of temperature and pressure, with negligible molecular volume and no intermolecular forces.
The square root of the average of the squares of the speeds of the individual molecules in a gas sample.
The gas constant per molecule, defined as $k = \frac{R}{N_A}$, equal to $1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}$.
Temperature measured on the Kelvin scale, starting from absolute zero where molecular motion theoretically ceases.
